thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU pool 'eu-west-1-gpu-pool-7' > 96% utilization for 7m. queue growth detected (queue_len 1900 -> 4350). autoscaler failing with repeated provider 429s. paging on-call.

maria_oncall: acked. i'm on it. joining bridge in 3. @ben_infra @tim_sre any immediate guesses? is this global or region-specific?

ben_infra: looks regional — eu-west-1 only. Dedicated tenants unaffected. host pools taking a huge burst, esp requests with long contexts. suspect single-tenant burst + model with long context windows.

tim_sre: quick tail of autoscaler logs (last 12m):
```
2026-03-20T21:04:12Z ERROR autoscaler: scaleup failed provider=cloudx code=429 msg="Too Many Requests"
2026-03-20T21:04:13Z INFO autoscaler: backoff -> 30s (attempts=1)
2026-03-20T21:05:44Z ERROR autoscaler: scaleup failed provider=cloudx code=429 msg="rate-limited"
2026-03-20T21:06:05Z WARN scalechain: op queue backlog=4200
2026-03-20T21:07:02Z INFO evictor: evicting best-effort pods count=140
```
provider seems to be throttling our scale calls, autoscaler retries pile up and then we end up with eviction thrash.

maria_oncall: ok. sara_ops — can you open provider case and also start a manual warm-pool? nate_prodeng, can you grab CS to check which customers are spiking?

sara_ops: opened ticket with provider — case ref CX-2026-03-20-09. launching emergency warm pool (reserved instances) in eu-west-1, ETA ~5m. will update.

nate_prodeng: calling CS now. june_support: can you surface top 10 tenants by qps in the last 15m?

june_support: top tenants: cust-7711, cust-9902, cust-4210. cust-9902 shows 6k concurrent short-chat sessions with ~5k token average. cs contacted cust-9902 ops; they are joining the bridge.

bridge-bot: BRIDGE CREATED -> https://meet.redwood/bridge/6481234567 (host: maria_oncall). reactions: :phone:

maria_oncall: joining bridge. tim — paste current autoscaler config that might cause synchronized retries.

tim_sre: snippet:
```
autoscaler:
  scale_up:
    step: 3
    max_per_minute: 6
    jitter: 0
    provider_retries: 4
```
no jitter + high per_minute + multiple retries = very bursty calls against provider.

ben_infra: yep that looks like it. also our metrics show token-per-request jumped ~3.8x for the last 10m.

cust-9902-rep (via bridge): we started a large customer-side campaign, sorry — we can throttle or pause. how long to stabilize?

maria_oncall: thanks for joining. if you can pause the campaign for ~7-10 minutes that will help while we bring warm capacity online.

cust-9902-rep: pausing now. confirming pause event.

tim_sre: mitigation plan executing:
- manual warm pool spin-up (sara_ops)
- reduce provider retries + add jitter to autoscaler (apply patch)
- enable aggressive eviction of best-effort / low-priority pods
- enable per-tenant shedding for non-SLA traffic
applying config change now.

ben_infra: manual scale requested via infractl:
```
$ infractl scale-pool eu-west-1-gpu-pool-7 --target 16 --force
request accepted id=prov-552982 queued
```
provider accepted but queued; warm pool still needed.

sara_ops: warm pool is online: +6 GPUs added from reserved pool. monitoring queues.

june_support: initial customer impact: ~11% of generation attempts returned 503/429 over last 12m, latency p95 increased to ~4.8s (baseline 1.2s). notifying affected enterprise customers.

maria_oncall: queue length: 4350 -> 1600 after pause + warm pool and config patch. throttles dropping inline with queue.

tim_sre: confirmed autoscaler patch applied: jitter=0.35, max_per_minute=2, provider_retries=1. also adding a provider-rate metric to alert on spikes of provider 429s.

nate_prodeng: moving to post-incident handoff. maria handing off to me. handoff_ts: 6481237890

nate_prodeng: ACTIONS documented (initial):
- A1: Add provider-aware jitter + exponential backoff cap to autoscaler (owner: tim_sre, due: 2026-03-27)
- A2: Implement tenant-level emergency throttle switch in routing layer (owner: ben_infra & june_support, due: 2026-03-24)
- A3: Automate warm-pool spin-up runbook and test (owner: sara_ops, due: 2026-03-30)
- A4: Add synthetic tenant-burst tests in perf lab simulating long-context churn (owner: eng-ml, assignee: lexi_ce, due: 2026-04-01)
- A5: Dashboard: per-tenant token-rate + provider-429 spike tile (owner: ben_infra, due: 2026-03-22)
- A6: Postmortem writeup and timeline (owner: nate_prodeng, due: 2026-03-23)

maria_oncall: timeline notes for postmortem: autoscaler first 429s at 6481234123, provider throttles peak 6481234300 - 6481234700, manual warm pool added at 6481234867, queue under threshold at 6481238800.

tim_sre: I'll open PR to change defaults and add telemetry: provider_429_per_min triggers an autoscaler slowdown policy.

ben_infra: adding runbook step: when provider 429s > X for Y minutes -> switch to queued warm pool + notify CS + trigger tenant-shed.

june_support: comms: notified customers cust-7711 and cust-9902, no legal escalation. cust-9902 agreed to pause and will update us on best-practices to avoid future blasts.

lexi_ce: will write synthetic load harness that can emulate single-tenant long-context bursts; will run against staging with warm-pool automation.

nate_prodeng: final severity: P2. impact: ~11% requests affected, two enterprise customers with transient errors, mitigated by customer pause + warm pool + autoscaler config change. recording for postmortem doc.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: queue stabilized, autoscaler defaults updated, bridge closed. reference -> /incidents/6481234567-postmortem

maria_oncall: thanks team. i'll add a short blameless note to the incident channel and link postmortem when Nate posts it.

nate_prodeng: capturing folks for follow-ups. tagging owners on action items. closing thread.
